subject: Genetics
title: Off-Target Effects
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Off-Target Effects.

hook.text: CRISPR sometimes cuts the wrong spot. In 3 billion letters, similar sequences exist. Friendly fire is real.

buildup.text: A guide RNA tolerates a few mismatches. Three billion letters guarantee some near-matches exist somewhere else.

discovery.text: Off-target cuts can disrupt essential genes or activate cancer pathways. For therapy, this risk must approach zero.

twist.text: High-fidelity Cas9 variants reduce off-target cuts 10,000-fold. Engineering made the scissors more precise over time.

climax.text: Whole-genome sequencing after editing now detects unintended changes. Safety verification became standard practice.

punchline.text: Perfect aim in 3 billion letters. Almost there.

quiz.question: How have scientists reduced CRISPR's off-target effects?
